title: I let Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude send me a daily morning briefing
excerpt: I set up daily morning briefings in Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude. Only one read my calendar and inbox and arrived on time.
content_html:
Published Nov 20, 2026, 8:45 AM EST

Haroun authors features for Android Police, covering Android, Samsung, Google, and AI. He first joined in 2021, writing more than 200 news stories before moving on to features and how-tos. A one-time OnePlus die-hard who genuinely couldn't stand Samsung, he's since done a full about-face — he now daily-drives a Galaxy S24 Ultra and keeps an S23+, S22+, and his old S20 within arm's reach, which gives him a lot of hardware to put through its paces.

He also holds a medical degree (MBBS) and has been obsessed with consumer tech for more than a decade. His work has appeared on How-To Geek and Android Authority. When he's not buried in Google's apps or a Samsung settings menu, he's trying to get his chess rating past 1500 or reading up on genetics and preventive medicine.

The first thing I do when I pick up my phone in the morning is check my emails.

I also check my day's events, note the weather (especially if I plan to go out later), and scan the headlines on my Discover page. But that's a lot of apps to see a few things.

Since many AI tools can connect to those apps and browse the web, I figured I could get all my important updates as an AI brief instead. But I wasn't sure which AI tool to use.

So I tested Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude. Here are the results.

The setup was pretty simple

Gemini and ChatGPT were slightly easier

I told all three chatbots to send me a 7 a.m. daily brief.

It included Chicago's weather forecast (and whether I need an umbrella or jacket), my Google Calendar events, the three most important unread emails, the top three tech news stories, and the first thing I should do for the day.

ChatGPT showed buttons in the chat to connect Gmail and Calendar. Gemini didn't need me to set up anything, since it's already connected to Google's apps.

Claude made me forget

Like ChatGPT, Claude suggested I connect Calendar. But it didn't provide the same buttons, so I needed to dig into the connector settings.

I got carried away setting up all three apps at once, and I forgot to do that. As a result, the next morning's brief didn't include any calendar info. I fixed it for subsequent days, though.

Interestingly, Claude set the brief for 6:44 a.m., because tasks set on the hour can run late when servers are busy.

Gemini was always on time with mostly empty briefings

It never read my Calendar or Gmail

I expected Gemini to breeze through this challenge, but it was underwhelming.

It sent all the briefs at exactly 7 a.m., never missing even by a minute. And that was the best thing about it.

The brief was hardly helpful. It said I didn't have any Calendar events, but that was false since I deliberately created events to test this properly.

The email section was just as bad. Gemini always returned an "API service configuration error." This was particularly disappointing, considering how good Gemini in Gmail is.

It also gave me nothing for my first daily action. It always defaulted to "Tackle your highest-priority task first," which is anything but inspiring.

But it makes sense. Without emails or events, it had nothing to anchor its advice to.

ChatGPT's briefs were packed but always late

It had actual data on all five sections

ChatGPT's briefs included all five parts of my request.

It showed my calendar events and picked important unread emails from my inbox. It also linked news stories to their sources.

It even integrated my events and emails when suggesting my first daily action. It asked me to consider renewing a subscription (from my Gmail inbox) before my event that morning.

That's the kind of everyday planning where ChatGPT beats Gemini.

It sent two briefs every morning

This was somewhat annoying.

Here's what happened. During the setup, I wanted to see how the chatbots reacted to changes.

In my original prompt, I made Chicago weather the first thing on the list. Then I sent a follow-up asking for my calendar events on top.

All three chatbots acknowledged the change. But for some reason, ChatGPT kept sending two briefs: one with weather on top and the other with my events on top.

ChatGPT's briefings also came at different times, and it seemed to get later each day. The first brief came at 7:18 a.m. on day 1, 7:32 a.m. on day 2, and 7:39 a.m. on day 3.

If you want on-time briefs, ChatGPT is not the one.

Claude's briefs covered everything that mattered

When connected, anyway

Claude's only weak brief was day 1, where I forgot to connect the calendar.

However, after I sorted that out, subsequent briefs carried all the information I requested.

Claude listed all my calendar events. It was also the only chatbot to highlight an email from an actual person on a particular day, unlike ChatGPT, which listed automated emails for that same day.

Its weather forecast was also the closest to Google's.

But the best part was how it combined everything to give me the most useful next steps.

One day, it suggested finishing an article before my 9 a.m. meeting so I could be well ahead of my 5 p.m. deadline. The next day, it told me to lock in my pitches before my 5 p.m. call.

That's exactly the kind of information I want in my briefs.

The only slight annoyance was the notification shade: Claude was the only one that never previewed the brief. It just said "Briefing sent" on the first two days.

By day 3, though, it started adding sources to its notification previews.

It still didn't highlight what the brief contained, but that wasn't a problem, since I would read the whole thing anyway.

Claude's briefs are definitely worth waking up to

I expected Gemini to ace this because a lot of the tasks depend on Google's tools: Gmail and Calendar. But it couldn't read those apps.

ChatGPT came close and is the best on a free plan, since Claude only offers scheduled briefings on its paid plans. But Claude was better overall, especially at integrating all the information it got.

If you don't mind Claude taking on more Google apps, it can also clean up your Drive when Gemini won't.
